draft.title: fix(gmail): preserve attachments carried in message body data
draft.issueTitle: [Bug]: Gmail attachments stored directly in body.data disappear from reads and forwards
draft.issueBody:
### Details

Gmail may return attachment bytes directly in MessagePartBody.data without an attachmentId. Orca only lists parts with an attachmentId and therefore silently drops these files when reading or forwarding messages.

## Reproduction

Read a Gmail message with three named parts: binary bytes in body.data without an attachmentId, an empty body.data attachment, and an external attachmentId. Invoke readGmail, downloadGmailAttachment and composeForward. All three files should remain present with their exact bytes and order; an unavailable part without data or an ID remains excluded.

Reproducible production-entry fixture: https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/blob/afloat16/orca50-20261127-gmail-inline-attachments/src/main/google/google-gmail-inline-attachments.test.ts

**Before:** The exact base production readGmail returned only remote.txt and omitted inline.bin and empty.txt.

**Expected and verified with the change:** Actual message reads list all three attachments; downloads and composeForward preserve exact binary, empty and external attachment bytes in order. Unavailable body data remains excluded.

Environment: Linux, Node 24.22.3, source checkout 9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817. The provider boundary uses real Response schemas and local protocol fixtures; no live Google account is claimed.

Primary API references:
- https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.messages.attachments
- https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.messages

Related work checked for distinct scope:
- #50497 and #50413 change bodyText MIME representation selection; their patches do not change attachmentsOf or downloadGmailAttachment.
- #48067 changes CLI save collision behavior, not Gmail attachment presence or retrieval.
draft.prTemplate:
## ELI5

Keep files Gmail already included in a message so reading, downloading and forwarding do not silently omit them.

## What Changed

Recognize named inline-data parts, including empty files, and download their existing bytes without calling the external-attachment endpoint. Preserve external-attachment reads and existing size checks.

## Why

Gmail may return attachment bytes directly in MessagePartBody.data without an attachmentId. Orca only lists parts with an attachmentId and therefore silently drops these files when reading or forwarding messages.

Production callers: readGmail exposes downloadable attachment references; downloadGmailAttachment serves CLI/RPC attachment downloads; composeForward and composeRevision retain existing message files through savedAttachments.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #ISSUE_NUMBER

## Visual Proof

N/A

This changes attachment data delivered by existing CLI/RPC operations, with no graphical layout or interaction control change.

| Same production input before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The exact base production readGmail returned only remote.txt and omitted inline.bin and empty.txt. | Actual message reads list all three attachments; downloads and composeForward preserve exact binary, empty and external attachment bytes in order. Unavailable body data remains excluded. |

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally through the actual production entries below
- [x] Automated regression added for external data integrity
- [x] The added regression fails against the original production code and uses the real operation with only provider responses supplied

Read a Gmail message with three named parts: binary bytes in body.data without an attachmentId, an empty body.data attachment, and an external attachmentId. Invoke readGmail, downloadGmailAttachment and composeForward. All three files should remain present with their exact bytes and order; an unavailable part without data or an ID remains excluded.

```sh
node config/scripts/test-runtime/execution-policy/run-vitest.mjs run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/google/google-gmail-inline-attachments.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

Integrated inline-attachment, existing forwarding-budget and MIME regressions:3files/5tests passed.

Final integrated validation: 32 focused regression tests in 22 files passed, including the unchanged archive-write failure case that had timed out under earlier heavy concurrent checking. The Drive performance contract passed separately (1 file/1 test). Changed-code quality passed with zero new findings across 129 changed paths; final touched-file formatting and git diff --check passed. Node typechecking passed for 17,026 files and web typechecking for 16,094 files using the repository-supported Bun compiler with one worker. These are aggregate validation results for the prepared contributions, not per-PR test counts.

The required `pnpm check:changed --base=9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817` was attempted after the final edits. Its workspace-package build is blocked because this environment rejects the tsx CLI local IPC socket (`listen EPERM`). The default tsrs typechecker was also terminated with SIGKILL; the supported Bun typechecking route completed successfully. The complete gate/build is not claimed to pass and still requires CI.

Linux was exercised locally. No live Google account, graphical desktop, macOS, Windows or SSH execution is claimed. The provider-neutral code remains on the existing runtime paths.

## Performance

Existing account/part validation and declared-size limit remain. Inline attachment bytes are already present in the full message response, so no additional external-attachment request is made. Remote attachment retrieval is unchanged. Recognizing previously omitted files also includes them in the existing aggregate forward-size check. No MIME body-representation changes.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

Previously omitted inline files are now included in downloads and forwarded drafts, so the existing aggregate size check may reject a draft that was previously incomplete. Account validation, external attachment retrieval and declared-size checks remain. No MIME text-representation change is included. A revert restores prior attachment detection; already saved files or sent messages are not altered.
